ridership: Over the 12 months to Oct 2026, systemwide recovery is uneven: Commuter Rail is at 91.0% of 2019 weekday ridership, buses at 84.6%, but the Red Line only 61.9%.
Best forecaster in a 12-origin rolling backtest: holt winters (MAPE 4.1% vs. seasonal-naive 7.1%).
reliability: Trailing-12-month bus on-time performance: worst route after Bayesian shrinkage is route 35 at 47.1% (90% CI 46.9%–47.4%).
Least reliable Commuter Rail line over the last 12 months: Franklin Line at 85.9% on time.
slow_zones: Slow zones peaked on 28 Mar 2023 at 38.2 restricted track-miles across 227 restrictions; on 31 Oct 2026 there were 0.18 miles (3 restrictions).
Heavy-rail riders lost 10,779,290 rider-hours to excess trip time in 2023 vs 2,644,156 in 2025 — a 75% reduction.
Each extra 1% of a line's track under restriction is associated with +0.160 excess minutes per rider-trip (95% CI 0.126–0.194, line fixed effects, n=135 line-months).
stations: Of 63 comparable gated stations, the slowest to recover is Davis (47.1% of 2019 weekday taps); the strongest is World Trade Center (113.5%).
Median recovery across the 15 busiest stations is 66.6% vs 69.5% across all comparable stations.
Excluded as fare-collection changes, not demand loss: Lechmere.
experience: In 2025 the MBTA posted 2,062 elevator outage alerts and 2,126 escalator outage alerts — 21,005 elevator-hours unavailable.
2025 passenger survey: 65.1% of riders meet the MBTA Title VI low-income definition, yet only 9.6% ride on any reduced fare and 74.4% pay full fare out of pocket (n=145,468).
fare_integrity: Optimised, randomised deployment of 32 inspector-hours deters 257% more evasion than an even spread and 54% more than busiest-station-first (k=3.0); across all 30 sensitivity cases the gain ranges 44%–687% vs uniform and 1%–281% vs busiest-first.

At the $2.40 fare, the MBTA's $50 citation deters a rational evader only if at least 4.8% of trips are checked — about 15,379 checks every weekday at gated stations alone. For scale, the MBTA reported 88 warnings and 0 citations for all of 2025.

Weighting exposure by the measured MBTA time-of-day evasion profile (evening 28% vs AM peak 19%) changes the optimal plan only marginally (+1.0%), so volume-based targeting is robust to the time-of-day pattern.

2025 gated entries (92.3M paid taps) imply between $6.8M and $32.5M a year of subway fare at risk if MBTA subway evasion sat anywhere between the 3% gated-system benchmark and New York's 2024 subway rate of 12.8% (scenario, not measurement).
8.5% of weekday gate entries happen 9pm–5am, when stations are least staffed.
short_hop: Today Copley → Arlington (1 stop, 0.6 km) and Copley → Medford/Tufts (13 stops, 9.7 km) both cost $2.40.
Distance fare with the whole line = $2.40: Heath Street → Medford/Tufts (13.8 km) pays $2.40; Copley → Medford/Tufts pays $1.68; Copley → Arlington pays the $0.80 minimum.
Minimum fare $0.80 = one third of the cap, Washington Metrorail's min:max ratio ($2.25–$6.75); Hyderabad's ratio (₹11–₹69) would give $0.38.
Trade-off: because lines differ in length (4.0 km to 28.4 km), 'whole line = $2.40' prices a kilometre between $0.08 and $0.59. A uniform-rate option is included for comparison.
Revenue break-even: a $0.80 short trip must grow paying riders on it by 200%; Copley → Medford/Tufts at $1.68 needs 43%. Pilot before system-wide rollout.
